facts: A volume boot record ( VBR ) is a type of boot sector introduced by the IBM Personal Computer.
A volume boot record ( VBR ) is also known as a volume boot sector.
A volume boot record ( VBR ) may be found on a partitioned data storage device or an unpartitioned device.
A volume boot record ( VBR ) contains machine code for bootstrapping programs stored in other parts of the device.
On non-partitioned storage devices, a volume boot record ( VBR ) is the first sector of the device.
On partitioned devices, a volume boot record ( VBR ) is the first sector of an individual partition on the device.
The code in volume boot records is invoked either directly by the machine's firmware or indirectly by code in the master boot record or a boot manager.
Invoking a VBR via a boot manager is known as chain loading.
Some dual-boot systems, such as NTLDR, take copies of the bootstrap code that individual operating systems install into a single partition's VBR.
Some dual-boot systems, such as NTLDR, load the relevant VBR content from file after the boot loader has asked the user which operating system to bootstrap.
NTLDR is the boot loader for all releases of Microsoft's Windows NT-derived operating systems up to and including Windows XP and Windows Server 2003.
In Windows Vista, Windows Server 2008 and newer versions, NTLDR was replaced.
In Windows Vista, Windows Server 2008 and newer versions, the boot-loader functionality is instead provided by two new components: WINLOAD.EXE and the Windows Boot Manager.

In file systems such as FAT12, FAT16, FAT32, HPFS and NTFS, the VBR also contains a BIOS Parameter Block ( BPB ) that specifies the location and layout of the principal on-disk data structures for the file system.
